title: Snag Chub Rub vs. Old Navy PowerSoft: Two Different Answers to Thigh Chafe
summary: One is a lightweight slip short meant to disappear under clothes; the other is an opaque eight-inch bike short with pockets. The better long-walk choice starts with the outfit, not the size label.
author: Curvy& Editorial

sections.heading: Do you need an underlayer or the outfit itself?
paragraphs: A recent r/PlusSizeFashion shopper asked for bicycle shorts that would survive long walks without riding up, overheating, or allowing thigh chafe. The replies surfaced two recurring but fundamentally different options: Snag's Chub Rub Shorts and longer bike shorts such as Old Navy's PowerSoft. Treating them as substitutes hides the most important decision.

Snag describes Chub Rub Shorts as a lightweight, moisture-wicking layer for wearing under dresses and skirts. Old Navy's current High-Waisted PowerSoft Biker Shorts are opaque activewear with an eight-inch inseam, phone pockets, and a fitted silhouette intended to be seen. Pick the clothing role first. A discreet layer beneath a dress and a standalone walking short are solving different comfort, coverage, and storage problems.

sections.heading: The fabrics create different kinds of hold
paragraphs: Snag uses a hosiery-like construction with a cotton gusset. Sizes A/B through E are listed as 94% polyamide, 5% elastane, and 1% cotton; the short F and G sizes use 89% polyamide, 10% elastane, and 1% cotton. The brand emphasizes cooling yarn, moisture wicking, and a light feel. Its product page does not publish an inseam, so shoppers cannot confirm exactly where the hem will land from the listing alone.

Old Navy's PowerSoft short uses 77% polyester and 23% spandex with a mesh-lined waistband. It has a defined eight-inch inseam, sits at the belly button, and includes the brand's Go-Dry wicking treatment. That heavier active construction should offer more compression and opacity than the Snag layer; it may also feel warmer under another garment. This is a construction-based comparison, not a guarantee that either hem will stay fixed on every thigh shape.

sections.heading: XXL does not convert directly to Snag G
paragraphs: Old Navy separates XXL from plus 2X even though its chart places both around size 20. XXL is listed at a 42-inch waist and 51.5-inch hip, while 2X covers sizes 20–22 with a 42-to-44.25-inch waist and 51.5-to-53.75-inch hip. That overlap is a reminder to use measurements and the exact product range rather than assuming identical letter sizes have identical shaping.

Snag uses a matrix combining clothing size, height, and body-shape guidance. The chart directs shoppers with a prominent bum or tum differently from those with a smaller or flatter bum or tum in some size-and-height combinations. US sizes 24–32 map to G, while sizes 16–22 can map differently. Enter the matrix from current measurements and proportions, not from an Old Navy label that happens to fit.

sections.heading: Ride-up is a geometry problem, not just a length problem
paragraphs: Community replies often favored hems around eight or nine inches over five-inch shorts for walking, because a longer hem may finish below the widest or highest-friction part of the thigh. That is a useful pattern to test, not a universal rule. A hem can still climb when it lands on a strong taper, when the leg opening is too loose, or when each stride asks the fabric to travel upward.

For the Old Navy pair, the published eight-inch inseam lets you measure the likely endpoint against a short you own. For Snag, ask the brand for the unstretched inseam in your proposed size, or order only if you are comfortable evaluating an unpublished length. Neither a high elastane percentage nor a brand's stay-put claim replaces a movement test on your body.

sections.heading: Test friction, temperature, and return risk together
paragraphs: Indoors, walk briskly, climb stairs, sit, and take several long strides while the tags remain attached. Check whether the hems migrate into the friction zone, the waistband rolls, sweat accumulates, or seams rub. Under a dress, also check whether the short catches the outer fabric. As a standalone short, confirm opacity in bright light and whether a loaded phone pocket changes the leg position.

Return rules change the risk of that experiment. Snag's FAQ gives eligible purchases a 90-day return period, but tights, Chub Rub Shorts, and intimate products can be returned only if they have not been tried on; return-label costs can also apply unless guaranteed returns were purchased. Old Navy offers free returns on qualifying items, while final-sale merchandise is excluded. Verify the status shown at checkout, because the lower-risk first test may be the product you can actually move in and still return.
bullets: Choose Snag when the priority is a light, discreet layer under a dress or skirt.
Choose PowerSoft when you want an opaque eight-inch outer short with pockets and firmer hold.
Measure the desired hem endpoint and read each brand's chart independently.

researchNote: This comparison begins with a September 2026 community request and verifies each current product's intended use, materials, sizing, and return constraints on official brand pages. Reports about ride-up are individual experiences; the underlayer-versus-activewear framework is an editorial comparison.
